help.title: Help
help.formats.title: Supported files
help.formats.body:
Import: STL mesh files, both ASCII and binary (the usual export of 3D-printing, scanning and modelling tools).
Export: STEP (.step) or IGES (.igs). Both open in SolidWorks, Creo, NX, Fusion 360, FreeCAD and other CAD software.
help.units.title: Size and units
help.units.body: STL files carry no units. The app converts the numbers as they are, without scaling. Most tools export STL in millimetres, so the CAD file is usually in millimetres too. If the part is 25.4 times too big or small, the STL was in inches: pick the right unit when importing into CAD.
help.step_iges.title: STEP or IGES?
help.step_iges.body:
STEP is the modern exchange format. The result is a solid you can measure, cut and fillet right away, so it is recommended.
IGES is older. The result is a set of surfaces that must be knitted/sewn into a solid in CAD. Choose it only if the other side needs IGES. IGES file info supports English characters only.
help.presets.title: The three presets
help.presets.body:
Recommended: the same algorithm as the desktop version (original mode). Fast, fine for most parts.
Smaller file: reduce faces to 50 %, then merge triangles lying on the same plane into one face. Much smaller files that are smoother in CAD, with slightly less detail.
Strict: “sewing” mode stitches neighbouring faces into a solid. More rigorous, usually somewhat slower. Use it for files with several parts, or when the recommended result is not a solid.
Any manual change in Advanced settings shows as “Custom”.
help.mode.title: Original vs sewing mode
help.mode.body:
Original: builds one shell and one solid directly from shared triangle edges. Same result as the desktop version, fast.
Sewing: turns every triangle into a face and stitches them within a tolerance. Handles small gaps and gives each part its own solid, but is slower and uses more memory.
help.merge.title: Merge coplanar faces
help.merge.body: In STL one flat face is usually many triangles. With merging on, triangles on the same plane become one CAD face. Parts with many flat faces (machined parts, sheet metal, housings) often shrink by half or more and are easier to select and measure in CAD. Curvy models (sculptures, scans) barely change and just take a little longer.
help.simplify.title: Why reduce faces?
help.simplify.body: Every triangle becomes a CAD face. More faces mean bigger files, slower conversion and a sluggish CAD session. Simplifying merges neighbouring triangles while keeping the shape. A lower ratio gives a smaller file but coarser fillets and lettering. Try 50 % first. The app suggests it for models above 200,000 faces.
help.meta.title: File info
help.meta.body: Author, organization, product and description are written into the file header and show up in CAD file properties. All empty by default. The timestamp is the current UTC time.
help.privacy.title: Privacy
help.privacy.body: All conversion happens on this device. Files are never uploaded and the app collects no usage data. Results are stored only on this device and are removed with the app.
help.faq.title: FAQ
help.faq.q1: Why does it open as surfaces, not a solid?
help.faq.a1: For IGES this is normal: IGES is a surface format, sew it in CAD or export STEP instead. For STEP it means the STL is not closed (it has holes). The done screen says so. Repair the mesh first, or try Strict.
help.faq.a2: Original mode puts all parts into one solid. Choose Strict (sewing) to get one solid per part.
help.faq.q3: Why is the file so big?
help.faq.a3: STEP is text and each triangle face takes dozens of lines. Merge coplanar faces or reduce faces.
help.faq.q4: Conversion is slow or the app quits
help.faq.a4: Very large meshes can run out of memory on a phone. Reduce faces first and keep the app in the foreground.
help.faq.q5: Chinese text disappeared from IGES file info
help.faq.a5: IGES supports English characters only. Other characters are removed. Use STEP to keep them.
help.faq.q6: How do I get the file onto my computer?
help.faq.a6: On the done screen tap Share… and send it via WeChat/QQ, AirDrop or mail, or save it to Files and sync with iCloud Drive.
help.estimate.title: Time and size estimates
help.estimate.body: Estimated from the face count and settings, shown as a range. Actual time depends on the device and the shape. Merging coplanar faces shrinks flat-faced parts a lot, so the range is wider.
